name: 祭祖
highlights: 一年中三个阴间节日：清明、冬至、中元
清明祭祖最隆重，前三天后四天到祖坟祭扫，添土标青
清明果有红白青三种，用馃印压制，最具特色
冬至以家庭为单位小型祭祖，祭拜前四代祖宗，做羹饭
中元（鬼节）也祭祖，同时祭祀孤魂野鬼，有路头羹饭
content_zh:
对祖先的祭祀活动一直是中国民众社会生活的重要组成部分，同时也是一种最淳朴的宗教意识的体现。人们通过一系列的丧葬仪式来安抚死者的灵魂，使他们能够顺利地进入另一个世界，并在那里安逸舒适的生活。仅仅这样还不够，人们还要借助定期供奉食物、送钱、送衣物的形式和祖先保持联系，祈求祖先保佑整个家族人丁兴旺，财源茂盛，五谷丰登。在一年中众多的节日里，有三个节日被认为是阴间的节日。在这三天里，村里都有或大或小的祭祖活动。

清明：祭祖仪式最隆重的要属清明，即每年的四月初。在清明的前三天、后四天，村里的人要到各房的祖坟上去祭扫，添土和标青，标青即是在坟前挂白纸。祭祀用的食物通常包括猪头、鹅、豆腐、糕、大麦面、金团和清明果等，其中以清明果最有特色。清明果有红、白、青三种，它是用糯米做皮，红糖或白糖做馅的点心。磨好的糯米直接用的话就可以做出白色的清明果；如果加入野菜汁（野蒿），就可以做成青色的；红色的则是加入了食用颜料。和其他地方不同的是，当地的清明果是借用馃印压制成的。金团类似于清明果，只是用豆腐、粉丝、青菜和猪肉做馅。

祭祀的过程是由在场的辈分最大的人主持，主持人通过高喊通和引来指挥其余的人。通是让大家准备好一起做事，而引则是让某个人前去祭拜。整个祭祀的程序大致包括拈香、点烛、跪拜、奠酒、进汤、献饭、读祝文和焚祝文，其中在焚祝文的同时还会打锣、吹号和放鞭炮。祭祀结束之后所有的人会在一起席地围坐吃午餐，又名散清。

岩下老街的程姓人中，如今多数是十五世毅庵公的后人。据民国33年（1944年）《程氏天房谱》记载，毅庵葬四十二都小墟塘龟山墈前墈下，距岩下村35里，现属舟山镇。因为距离远，坐轿子单程要走三四个小时，再加上开销大（雇轿子的费用由个人出一半，祖上出一半），所以每年去的人不多，一般也只有四五十人左右。能去的人多来自地位较高和家境较好的人家，而且妇女和外姓人也可以去。已经年过古稀的程镇康老先生回忆说，他小时候随父亲去过舟山两次祭祖。让他印象最深的就是：经过的村庄都会觉得这四五十顶轿子组成的队伍很是威风。这在客观上也是对岩下程氏的一种宣传，使邻村的姑娘都愿意嫁到这样的望族。程毅庵的夫人被子孙们尊称为太婆。因为她葬在较近的金龙江，每年清明去的人就较多。

村里的一部分人还会到下胡坑里作勳公的坟地去拜天官。作勳公是岩下程氏第十三世上的人，岩上村的作勳公祠也是以他命名的。他之所以受到如此尊敬，是因为他性情敦朴，节俭持躬，铢积寸累以成家业。而资雄里闬，每遇岁歉必出粟赈饥，凡有求者缓急靡不相济。人皆德之。

在清明那天，村里的几个祠堂会打开祠堂门，挂起祖宗像，摆上猪头、鹅、豆腐等供品，等待子孙们的祭拜。比起那些有钱有地位的人，村里那些穷苦的程氏后人就只能在清明那天到祠堂里去拜拜祖宗，期待着可以分到的那点供品。现住在作勳公祠里，74岁的程茂发老人讲：他在十六岁以后就可以去祠堂祭祖，并且他有三个祠堂可以去。他可以从村里人人都有份的世远公祠和一部分人有份的作勳公祠里各领到一斤饭、两片肉和两片豆腐；他还能从本房的，一个在几家人中轮换管理的祠堂里领到一点钱。

1995年，永康程氏第一到第四世祖的墓被统一移到了离村子三里的北政岭。自此，遍布永康地区十七个村的程氏后人开始在清明期间进行联合祭祖。祭祖的活动由十七个村庄的程氏轮流主持，通常情况下是由村里老年协会的主席带头组织。

冬至：冬至是另外一个祭祀祖先的重要时间。不同于清明时期的宗族集体祭祖，冬至主要是以家庭为单位进行小型的祭祖活动，祭拜的对象通常也仅限于自家前四代的祖宗。在清光绪编《永康县志》中提道旧家大族四时祭于祖庙，而冬至祭最重。或许是因为冬至祭最重，所以住在岩下老街的程氏后人在四时之中只保留了冬至祭祖的习俗。当地人称冬至为下世人过年。在岩下老街和橙麓村里，关于冬至祭祖的时间有两种说法：一种说法是在冬至的当天祭祖；另一种说法则认为要在冬至的前三天或后四天中的一天中祭祖。但是他们祭祖的形式都是相似的。每一家都要做羹饭，在厅堂里摆供品以招待先祖。据程崇舜老人讲，冬至祭祖的羹饭要比其他日子里的多一些点心。

祭祀过程多在午饭之前，有的人家还会放鞭炮。岩下街79号的程镇康家每年都在冬至这天祭祖，2008年冬至这天他家的供桌上摆了猪肉、煎豆腐、鸡蛋、自家种的橘子和用糯米做皮，豆腐、粉丝、猪肉和青菜做馅的团子。这些供品放在桌子中间，旁边整整齐齐的摆放了九副碗筷和酒杯。在靠近明堂一侧的桌子上有两个烛台和两束各三支的香。在一切都准备好以后，程家的女主人，即程镇康的夫人，拿着一束香到院门口拜三拜请祖宗们回家。如果这时外面正好有人的话，大家都会自觉地让开门口。等祖宗们落座之后，程家的儿子要给每个祖宗敬三次酒，酒是用自家酿的上好黄酒。随后，家里的人开始在院子里一起给祖宗烧些纸钱和纸银锭。最后，程家的女主人要拿着另一束香，走到门口再拜三拜送祖宗们回去，然后关上院门。在整个祭祀过程结束之后，供桌上的部分美味就成了当日午餐的一部分。

中元：第三个祭祖的日子是在阴历七月十五的中元节，也称鬼节。在这一天里，家家户户也要做羹饭来盛筵祖先。但是不同于另外两个节日的是，在这一天，短命的和没有后代的孤魂野鬼也可以享受到祭祀。正如县志里说：中元，荐祖考、祀孤。所以这里有些善良的人家会在祭祖之后，用篮子带上一些供品，到村庄外的路口或者空地上进行野祭，俗称路头羹饭。更有富裕的人家会结队去寺院或是祠堂去拜星，以超度饿鬼和死囚。这一切都是为了能让自己的祖先安心地享受儿孙们孝敬的香烛、食物和钱财，而不会被那些受不到祭祀的孤魂野鬼骚扰。
content_en:
Ancestor sacrifice has always been an important part of Chinese social life and a manifestation of the simplest religious consciousness. Through funeral rituals, people soothe the souls of the dead, enabling them to enter another world and live comfortably there. Beyond this, people maintain contact with ancestors through regular offerings of food, money, and clothing, praying for prosperous descendants, wealth, and abundant harvests. Among the many festivals in a year, three are considered festivals of the underworld, with ancestor worship activities of varying scale in the village.

Qingming: The most solemn ancestor worship is at Qingming, in early April. From three days before to four days after, villagers visit the graves of each branch to sweep, add soil, and biao qing (mark green)—hanging white paper before the grave. Sacrificial foods typically include pig head, goose, tofu, cake, barley flour, jin tuan (golden dumplings), and qingming guo (Qingming cakes), with the latter being most distinctive. Qingming guo come in red, white, and green varieties, made with glutinous rice skin and brown or white sugar filling. White is made with plain ground rice; green with wild vegetable juice (wild mugwort); red with food coloring. Uniquely, local qingming guo are pressed using a guo mold. Jin tuan are similar but filled with tofu, glass noodles, greens, and pork.

The ceremony is led by the most senior person present, who commands tong (prepare together) and yin (individual to worship). The procedure includes lighting incense and candles, kneeling, pouring wine, offering soup and rice, reading and burning the prayer text—with gongs, horns, and firecrackers during the burning. Afterward, everyone sits together on the ground for lunch, called san qing (dispelling Qingming).

Most Cheng surnamed people on the old street are descendants of the 15th generation Yi'an Gong. According to the 1944 Cheng Family Tian Branch Genealogy, Yi'an is buried at Turtle Mountain in Xiaxutang, 35 li from Yanxia, now in Zhoushan Town. Due to the distance—a three-to-four-hour sedan chair ride each way—and high cost (half paid by individuals, half by the ancestors), only about 40-50 people go each year, mostly from well-off families; women and outsiders may also attend. Elder Cheng Zhenkang recalls going twice as a child; the 40-50 sedan chairs made an imposing procession through villages, effectively advertising the Yanxia Cheng clan and attracting brides from neighboring villages. Yi'an's wife, honored as Tai Po, is buried closer at Jinlong River, so more people visit her grave.

Some villagers visit the grave of Zuoxun Gong in Xiahu Pit to bai tianguan (worship the heavenly official). Zuoxun Gong, the 13th generation of Yanxia Cheng, has an ancestral hall named after him in Yanshang village. He is revered for his simple and frugal character, accumulating wealth gradually, and distributing grain during famines—all who sought help received it.

On Qingming day, several ancestral halls open their doors, hang ancestor portraits, and display pig head, goose, and tofu offerings. Poorer Cheng descendants can only visit the halls to worship and hope for a share of offerings. 74-year-old Cheng Maofa, who lives in Zuoxun Gongci, says he could worship at three halls after age 16: Shiyuan Gongci (everyone's share) and Zuoxun Gongci (partial share) each gave him one jin of rice, two slices of meat, and two slices of tofu; his own branch's hall, managed in rotation among several families, gave a little money.

In 1995, the graves of the first through fourth generation Cheng ancestors were moved to Beizheng Ridge, three li from the village. Since then, Cheng descendants across 17 Yongkang villages hold joint Qingming worship, rotated among the villages and usually led by the village seniors' association chair.

Winter Solstice: Another important time for ancestor worship. Unlike the clan collective worship at Qingming, Winter Solstice is mainly small family-based worship, usually limited to the previous four generations. The Guangxu-era Yongkang County Gazetteer notes that old prominent families sacrificed at ancestral temples in all four seasons, but Winter Solstice sacrifice was the most important. Perhaps because of this, Yanxia Cheng descendants retained only Winter Solstice worship among the four seasons. Locals call Winter Solstice the underworld people's New Year. There are two views on timing: the day itself, or one day within three days before or four days after. The form is similar: each family makes geng fan (thick rice meal) and sets out offerings in the main hall. According to Elder Cheng Chongshun, Winter Solstice geng fan includes more snacks than other days.

The ceremony usually takes place before lunch, sometimes with firecrackers. At Cheng Zhenkang's home (No. 79 Yanxia Street), the 2008 Winter Solstice offering table had pork, fried tofu, eggs, homegrown oranges, and glutinous-rice dumplings filled with tofu, glass noodles, pork, and greens. Nine sets of bowls, chopsticks, and wine cups were neatly arranged. Two candle holders and two bundles of three incense sticks each stood on the side toward the courtyard. After preparation, the lady of the house took incense to the courtyard gate, bowed three times to invite ancestors home. After the ancestors were seated, the son offered wine three times to each ancestor, using home-brewed fine yellow wine. The family then burned paper money and silver ingots in the courtyard. Finally, the lady took another bundle of incense to the gate, bowed three times to send the ancestors back, and closed the gate. Part of the offerings became lunch.

Zhongyuan (Ghost Festival): The third ancestor worship day is the 15th of the seventh lunar month, also called Ghost Festival. Every household makes geng fan for ancestors. Unlike the other two festivals, on this day short-lived and descendantless wandering ghosts also receive sacrifice. As the gazetteer says: Zhongyuan, offer to ancestors and sacrifice to the lonely. Kind families take offerings in baskets to crossroads or open spaces outside the village for wild sacrifice, called lutou gengfan (roadside thick rice meal). Wealthier families go in groups to temples or ancestral halls to bai xing (worship stars), transcending hungry ghosts and condemned prisoners. All this ensures that ancestors can enjoy offerings undisturbed by wandering ghosts.
